sections.html:
Ogden is the Weber County seat, about 40 miles north of Salt Lake City and 10 miles east of the Great Salt Lake. Its 27.55 square miles climb from the valley floor to the Wasatch foothills at about 4,341 feet. The city has six districts: the North End takes in West Ogden, Downtown and East Central, and the East side holds the East Bench and Shadow Valley. South Ogden, Roy, West Haven, Marriott-Slaterville, Farr West, Harrisville, Pleasant View and North Ogden are neighbors.

The 2020 count was 87,321 people in 33,508 households. Owners occupy 61.3% of homes, the median home value is $355,600, median gross rent is $1,216 and median household income is $72,575. The average trip to work takes 22.5 minutes.

Historic districts include Historic 25th Street, Eccles Avenue and Jefferson Avenue, and landmarks include Union Station, Peery's Egyptian Theatre and the Ogden Nature Center. Over 44 percent of the city's housing was built before 1940, so an older house with original wiring, plumbing or a tired roof is common here.

Newer construction is arriving too. The city approved Lotus Riverwalk Phase 2 with 174 units, Meadowbrook with 48 and Capital Square with 176 as moderate-income housing projects, and the R-9 zone in the 9 Rails Creative District allows up to 29 units per acre. Cottage lots of 1,500 square feet are allowed within two blocks of the bus rapid transit route.

sections.h2: Which school district is your Ogden address in?
sections.html: Ogden City School District follows the city limits exactly. Weber School District serves areas outside the city, even for homes that carry an Ogden mailing address, so the word Ogden in a listing does not tell a buyer which district applies. The city district runs Ogden High School and Ben Lomond High School, three junior highs (Highland, Mound Fort and Mount Ogden) and 13 elementary schools. DaVinci Academy of Science and the Arts is a charter school, and Saint Joseph Catholic High School is a private option.

sections.h2: Trains, buses and getting out of town
sections.html: FrontRunner links Ogden Central Station straight to Salt Lake City and on to Provo. The OGX bus runs between the station and Weber State University, and other UTA routes reach Brigham City, Weber County and Davis County. Ogden-Hinckley Airport is Utah's busiest municipal airport, and Breeze Airways flies the only commercial route, nonstop to Orange County, California.

Summers run hot and fairly dry, with highs often near 95 degrees, while winters bring snow from late October or early November until about April. Annual precipitation is 16.36 inches, and the roof and furnace of an older house feel both extremes.

The Weber segment of the Wasatch Fault last produced a major quake roughly 200 to 700 years ago, and active segments can reach about magnitude 7.5. If your house is old, a structural check before you list is worth considering.

Every residential rental in Ogden needs a license, and it is unlawful to occupy an unlicensed one. Applications go by email to businesslicense@ogdencity.com. An invoice follows, and the license is issued only after payment.

Short-term rentals face tighter limits under city code 15-13-38.

  • A sale voids a short-term rental license unless the new owner gets a new one within 90 days and before operating.
  • In R-1 zones only owner-occupied rentals are allowed, and a non-owner-occupied rental in a residential zone needs three years of continuous ownership.
  • Non-owner-occupied units are inspected every two years, and a revoked property is barred from short-term use for three years.
  • Occupancy is capped at two people per sleeping room, and parking must be on site.

If your house has been an Airbnb, check the license status before a buyer's agent does.

Weber County bills Ogden property taxes, and value is fixed as of January 1. The county follows the same yearly rhythm.

StepUsual timing
Valuation notices mailedAbout July 20
Appeal deadlineSeptember 15, within 45 days of the notice
Tax notices mailedAround October 17
Pay without penaltyBy November 30
Delinquent, penalty appliedDecember 1, the greater of 1% or $10
Interest beginsFebruary 1, retroactive to January 1

Send appeals to the Clerk/Auditor at 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 320. The valuation notice comes with an application. Tax relief shows up on the tax notice, not the valuation notice.

If the notice value looks too high, act inside the window. The notice arrives with an application attached. Fill it out, add whatever backs up your number, and deliver it to the Clerk/Auditor on Washington Blvd before September 15, or within 45 days of the notice if that is sooner. Evidence that tends to carry weight includes recent sales of similar houses nearby and repair estimates for defects an assessor could not see from the street. A seller who is already under contract may not bother, but the tax bill still follows the parcel until the deed is recorded.

Property taxes are billed to the owner of record, and the bill for the year of your sale is usually divided between you and the buyer on the closing statement. If November 30 is close, ask the title company whether the current bill has been paid. A delinquent balance does not stop a sale, but it will be paid from your proceeds. Penalty and interest grow on the schedule in the table above, so clearing it early costs less.

The Weber County Recorder charges $45 for the first page of a recording and nothing for additional pages. Each description over ten adds $2. Your title company will usually pay these fees at closing and file the deed.

sections.h2: Selling an Ogden house for cash
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the listing, the buyer's loan and the appraisal. You tell us about the house, we make an offer based on its condition, and a title company handles signing and recording.

Ogden owners often hold older houses, rentals or inherited property, and some still carry a rental license or a short-term rental permit. Send us those details first and we can talk through how they affect the sale before any offer. If the house is a former short-term rental, a new owner cannot simply continue under your license, so expect the buyer to ask about it.

Closing day is yours to pick with the title company. Bring a photo ID, the deed or estate papers if the house was inherited, and a payoff figure if a loan remains. Walk-throughs are short, and no one will ask you to paint, patch or haul away furniture.

faqs.q: What is the population of Ogden, Utah?
faqs.a: Ogden had 87,321 residents in 2020. The estimate shown at the top of this page is the more recent figure.

faqs.q: When are Weber County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the deadline to pay without penalty. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, with a penalty of the greater of 1 percent or $10.

faqs.q: Is every Ogden address in Ogden City School District?
faqs.a: No. The city district follows the city limits, while Weber School District serves areas outside it even when the address says Ogden.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out a house in Ogden?
faqs.a: Yes, every residential rental needs one, and it is unlawful to occupy an unlicensed rental. Short-term rentals carry extra limits, including a 90-day window for a new owner after a sale.

faqs.q: What are Ogden's older housing options like for sellers?
faqs.a: Over 44 percent of Ogden's housing was built before 1940. A cash buyer takes those houses as they are, so original systems and old roofs do not have to be repaired first.
